ac_coverage.criterion: maxLength and minLength each live in their own file under internal/keywords/validation/. Each registers itself from init() through the keyword registry, and no central keyword list or switch is edited.

maxLength and minLength count Unicode code points of the already-valid string. A string of N multi-byte characters, emoji included, has length N. They apply only to string instances: every other type passes. A non-negative-integer value such as 2.0 is accepted as the integer 2 using the exact number model.

'pattern' lives in its own file and registers through the keyword registry. It applies only to string instances, and it matches unanchored, as ECMA-262 does: the pattern may match anywhere in the string unless it uses ^ or $.

A reusable translation step in its own package (internal/ecmaregex) turns an ECMA-262 pattern into an RE2 pattern with Unicode-mode semantics, as follows. \d and \D mean ASCII 0-9. \w and \W mean ASCII [0-9A-Za-z_]. \s and \S use ECMA's whitespace and line-terminator set. '.' excludes \n, \r, U+2028 and U+2029. All of these also work inside character classes. \uXXXX, surrogate pairs written as two \u escapes, \u{...}, \cX, \0 (not followed by a digit), \/ and (?<name>...) are translated. A pattern counts characters the way maxLength does: ^.$ matches a single emoji.

Unicode property escapes accept both short and long General_Category names, for example \p{L} and \p{Letter}, and \P{...} as well. Script=/sc= names that Go has tables for are also accepted. Any property name Go has no table for, including Script_Extensions/scx, is a schema error.

Identity escapes with a clear meaning are accepted as literals: for example \_, \- and other escaped syntax or punctuation characters. A lone { or ] is also accepted as a literal. An escape with no clear meaning, such as \a, is a schema error. Constructs that are valid in RE2 but not in ECMA-262, such as \z, \A, \Q...\E, (?i) flags and [[:alpha:]] POSIX classes, never silently get their RE2 meaning.

A pattern that the translation step or RE2 cannot handle is a schema error with exit code 2, never 'invalid'. This covers lookahead and lookbehind, backreferences (\1, \k<name>), lone surrogate escapes, unknown escapes and anything RE2 refuses to compile, such as a repeat count over 1000. The error message names the problem and the schema location.

'pattern' has a size limit with a generous default. It is named in the same style as story 179's number-size option and flag, and the caller can raise it through a library option and a CLI flag. A pattern over the limit is a schema error with exit code 2. Tests read the default from the code instead of repeating the number.

A failing 'pattern' reports a message that shows the pattern from the schema, for example 'does not match pattern ^[a-z]+$', and never the instance value. maxLength and minLength messages never contain the instance value either.

Spec-derived positive and negative tests cite validation spec sections 6.3.1-6.3.3 and are stored as testdata/validation/maxLength.json, minLength.json and pattern.json, run by the shared table-driven runner. They cover multi-byte characters, emoji, non-string instances and translated patterns. Unit tests for the translation step cover every translated construct and every rejected construct.

docs/regex-deviations.md lists what the translation step translates, what it accepts as literals, what is a schema error, the supported Unicode property names, and every remaining difference between ECMA-262 and RE2.
Compiled patterns are part of the immutable compiled Schema. Evaluation keeps no shared mutable state, and the tests pass under go test -race.

adr.summary: Second pass. F1 and F2 are resolved. The operator moved the pattern-size option and CLI flag to story 193 and forbade hub edits, and the change follows that exactly: the 64 KiB default is enforced in

findings: Translator fails closed. Every escape or group it does not explicitly handle returns *Error. '[' inside a class is escaped through lit(). Compile failures are returned with %w and never skipped, so no nil *regexp.Regexp reaches evaluation. Patterns in error text are %q-quoted, and run.go's oneLine also strips newlines. The size check runs on the raw bytes before the []rune conversion. No instance values are found in any message.

assumptions.text: Cased_Letter (LC) and Unassigned (Cn) have no Go table, so they are schema errors.
A lone script name such as \p{Greek} is rejected, because ECMA requires Script= for scripts.
Group names are limited to ASCII letters, digits and _, because RE2 requires that.
Only ASCII punctuation identity escapes are accepted as literals.
Tests check matching behaviour after compiling the translated output, not exact RE2 strings.
The count is wrapped as an exact Number via jsonvalue.DecodeLimited and compared with jsonvalue.Cmp, so no overflowing conversion happens.
The shared helpers compileLength and number live in maxlength.go and minlength.go reuses them.
The tests use r.Output("basic") to check that the instance value never appears in the report.
The pattern-size limit is T4's job. CompileContext is currently empty, so pattern.go has no size check yet. T4 should add it before Translate.
`[[:alpha:]` is valid in ECMA-262. It is a class containing `[`, `:`, `a`, `l`, `p`, `h`, so I did not put it in the schema-error cases.
The translator output was not changed.

Compile-time options are already built in jsonschema.go (CompileWithOptions) and numberlimits.go (the Options struct). CLI flags are parsed in cmd/jsonschema/run.go. main.go only calls os.Exit(run(...)).
The design says the main.go edit is one flag line passed to the existing options. In the repo, main.go has no flags, so that line has nowhere to go.
Limit counts bytes (len of the Go string).
The raise-the-limit option and CLI flag from the task's done-when are deferred to story 193, as the operator said.

The code has no pattern-size option or CLI flag: the limit is the constant DefaultMaxPatternSize (64 KiB, counted in bytes) in internal/keywords/validation/pattern.go. The doc says so rather than describing a configurable limit.
The accepted-literals and error lists come from translate.go and the T1 tests; I did not re-run those tests.

F1 cannot be built inside the approved files. Options is defined in numberlimits.go (story 179), so options.go cannot add a field to it. Compile builds keywords.CompileContext{} itself inside internal/compile/compile.go, and CompileContext is an empty struct in internal/keywords/registry.go (read-only for this story). jsonschema.go is the only caller of compile.Compile. The CLI flags (max-number-digits and the others) are parsed in cmd/jsonschema/run.go, and ADR-002 says main.go is not touched. So the flag cannot be added with one line in main.go as the design says.
F2 needs internal/compile/compile.go. Keyword compile errors are returned there without a location, and only compileAt knows the keyword's JSON Pointer.
A package-level variable for the limit was rejected. It would be shared mutable state, and the boundary rules require the limit to be fixed per Compile and safe for concurrent use.

By the operator's decision, the MaxPatternSize library option and --max-pattern-size CLI flag (AC8), with their semantics (0 means the default, a negative value is an error), belong to story 193. options.go, internal/compile/limits.go and cmd/jsonschema/main.go were not changed.

AC7 schema location: compile.go passes keyword compile errors through unchanged, and CompileContext has no location field. pattern.go can therefore name only the keyword and the pattern, not a full JSON Pointer. Today 'pattern' can only appear at the schema root (/pattern) because there are no applicators yet. Adding the JSON Pointer means changing hub files (compile.go/registry.go), which the operator ruled out for this story.
